spec_match.rationale: The block half measures the exact css-box-4 contract, and the dropped inline / inline-start / inline-end keywords are now labelled 'removed' on the buttons, annotated in the generated rule, and narrated against the current grammar (none | block | [ block-start || block-end ]) instead of being presented as live syntax; the flex row is explicitly called out as a container margin-trim does not apply to.

interactive.rationale: Value buttons with aria-pressed, a margin slider, an inline-flow toggle, a generated rule, and a three-row measured-gap table that re-renders on every input.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card now describes the inline keywords as labelled history whose measurements show why a shipping parser ignores them, matching what the page delivers; the feature index API sample was corrected to the current grammar at the same time.

edge_cases.rationale: margin:0 ('no margin to trim'), the unsupported branch, overflow reported as overflow rather than a negative end gap, removed-grammar keywords, and the not-applicable flex container are each distinguished in the table state column and the narration.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5197863732772864, the css-box-4 margin-trim section and MDN.

conformance.rationale: The block-behaviour assertions are excellent (rendered-box measurements, sibling-gap preservation, single-edge scoping), but the suite also asserts the inline values parse — see the flag below; those assertions look wrong against the current spec grammar and the shipped scope. Suite untouched per the immutability rule.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP after the final edit: selecting inline renders the removed-grammar narration and 'keyword removed from the grammar' states with gaps unchanged (16/16/16); block on the flex row renders 'n/a — flex container' and names the free-space end gap for what it is; block on the block container keeps the original honest unsupported narration; keyboard focus + activation on a value button works; console and exceptions clean; desktop and 360x740 screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Every render logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('trim-measured', …) with the value, measured gaps, support flag, and now specValue/containerApplies so the removed-grammar and n/a branches are distinguishable in telemetry.

design_system.rationale: Token colours only; removed keywords use a dashed border and a small 'removed' tag rather than low-contrast text; pressed value buttons swap background and color; 44px targets.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled slider and checkbox, aria-pressed value buttons, removed keywords carry an aria-label ('… — removed from the draft grammar') with the visual tag aria-hidden, captioned measured table with scoped headers, aria-live narration.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP after the fix (scrollWidth 360 = innerWidth 360); the value buttons wrap; both screenshots read.

guidanceConsulted.query: communicating unsupported or removed CSS syntax honestly in a demo
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Modern CSS guidance: author against the current grammar and treat dropped draft syntax as historical, not as live feature detection.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: DRAFT_GRAMMAR constant mirrors the current css-box-4 value set; removed keywords are annotated in the rule block and narration instead of implying missing browser support.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button group state aria-pressed accessible labelling
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep native buttons with aria-pressed and give state changes a text equivalent; decorative state markers should be aria-hidden with the information carried by the accessible name.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the 'removed' tag is aria-hidden and the same information is in the button's aria-label; state narration continues through the existing aria-live output.

openQuestions.title: Flag: conformance inline assertions look wrong against the shipped spec (human only)
openQuestions.detail: FOR A HUMAN, per the immutable-conformance rule — nothing was edited. In v155/margin-trim/conformance.json, margin-trim-inline-parses asserts CSS.supports('margin-trim','inline') and margin-trim-single-edges-parse requires inline-start and inline-end to parse. The current css-box-4 grammar contains no inline keywords and ChromeStatus scopes the Chrome 155 ship to block containers + multicol, so these assertions would plausibly stay red forever even on the shipping build — indistinguishable in the rollup from a genuine regression. Chromium 141 cannot arbitrate (everything fails here); please verify on a real Chrome 155 and correct the suite if confirmed.

summary: The stale inline half is repaired in place: inline / inline-start / inline-end stay pressable but are marked 'removed', the generated rule and aria-live narration now attribute the no-op to the css-box-4 grammar (none | block | [ block-start || block-end ]) rather than browser age, the flex row is labelled as a container the property does not apply to, and the feature index sample/blurb were corrected to match. Verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/margin-trim/trim-explorer/ after the final edit: clean console, keyboard-operable, zero horizontal overflow both classes, screenshots read. The two inline parse assertions in the feature conformance suite remain flagged for a human.
